canonical_task: AGAP is P-complete (canonical alternating-reachability)
citation: Greenlaw, Hoover & Ruzzo, Limits to Parallel Computation: P-Completeness Theory (1995)

canonical_task: LFMM is P-complete (edge object, distinct from LFMIS)
citation: Miyano (1990); GHR (1995)

canonical_task: unit resolution / unit-clause propagation is P-complete
citation: GHR (1995); cf. Jones & Laaser (1976)

canonical_task: sandpile prediction is P-complete in dimension >= 3
citation: Moore & Nilsson, The computational complexity of sandpiles, J. Stat. Phys. 96 (1999)

canonical_task: LZ78 dictionary membership is P-complete
citation: De Agostino & Storer (1996)

canonical_task: grammar productivity closure, poly-time
citation: Jones & Laaser, Complete problems for deterministic polynomial time, TCS 3 (1976)

canonical_task: FAS decision: acyclic after removing <= k arcs?
citation: Karp, Reducibility among combinatorial problems, in Complexity of Computer Computations (1972) 85-103
note: one of Karp's 21. Distinct from feedback-arc-set-tournament (restriction, S2) and directed-feedback-vertex-set (arcs vs vertices, S2); Maximum Acyclic Subgraph is the complement -> MERGES here (S2)

canonical_task: Achromatic Number decision: psi(G) >= k?
citation: Bodlaender, Achromatic number is NP-complete for cographs and interval graphs, Inform. Process. Lett. 31 (1989) 135-138; general graphs: Yannakakis & Gavril (1980); trees: Cairnie & Edwards (1997)
note: NP-complete on cographs/interval graphs (Bodlaender 1989) establishes general NP-completeness; NP-complete even for trees (Cairnie-Edwards 1997)

canonical_task: Betweenness decision: a total order realizing every betweenness triple?
citation: Opatrny, Total ordering problem, SIAM J. Comput. 8 (1979) 111-114
note: NP-complete (Opatrny 1979). Distinct from Cyclic Ordering (cyclic vs total) and from Max-Betweenness (S2)

canonical_task: Closest String decision: a center string within Hamming distance d of all inputs?
citation: Frances & Litman, On covering problems of codes, Theory Comput. Syst. 30 (1997) 113-119; Lanctot, Li, Ma, Wang & Zhang (1999)
note: NP-complete even over a binary alphabet (Frances-Litman 1997). Distinct from Closest Substring (substring vs full string) and Closest String with wildcards (S2)

canonical_task: Cyclic Ordering decision: a circular order realizing every ordered triple?
citation: Galil & Megiddo, Cyclic ordering is NP-complete, Theoret. Comput. Sci. 5 (1977) 179-182
note: NP-complete (Galil-Megiddo 1977). Distinct from Betweenness (total vs cyclic order) (S2)

canonical_task: Firefighter decision: can >= k vertices be saved? NP-complete even on trees of max degree 3
citation: Finbow, King, MacGillivray & Rizzi, The firefighter problem for graphs of maximum degree three, Discrete Mathematics 307 (2007) 2094-2105
note: NP-complete on trees; general graphs NP-hard a fortiori

canonical_task: Graph Burning decision: b(G) <= k? NP-complete even on trees/forests and disjoint paths
citation: Bessy, Bonato, Janssen, Rautenbach & Roshanbin, Burning a graph is hard, Discrete Applied Mathematics 232 (2017) 73-87

canonical_task: Interval Completion decision: reach an interval graph by adding <= k edges? NP-complete
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979)
note: minimum interval graph completion is NP-complete [GT35-adjacent]; related to profile/pathwidth minimization

canonical_task: max-sum p-dispersion decision: p points with pairwise-distance sum >= D? NP-complete
citation: Hassin, Rubinstein & Tamir, Approximation algorithms for maximum dispersion, Operations Research Letters 21 (1997) 133-137
note: NP-hard (cf. Erkut, The discrete p-dispersion problem, EJOR 46 (1990) 48-60)

canonical_task: Maximum Planar Subgraph decision: a planar subgraph with >= k edges? NP-complete
citation: Garey & Johnson, Computers and Intractability (1979)
note: [GT27] Maximum Planar Subgraph; cf. Liu & Geldmacher 1979

canonical_task: Minimum Consistent DFA decision: a consistent DFA with <= k states?
citation: Gold, Complexity of automaton identification from given data, Information and Control 37 (1978) 302-320

canonical_task: Minimum Sum Coloring decision: a proper coloring of color-sum <= S?
citation: Bar-Noy, Bellare, Halldórsson, Shachnai & Tamir, On chromatic sums and distributed resource allocation, Inform. Comput. 140 (1998) 183-202
note: NP-hard on general graphs (chromatic sum; Kubicka-Schwenk 1989, Bar-Noy et al. 1998)

canonical_task: Node Multiway Cut decision: <= k non-terminal vertices separating all terminals?
citation: Dahlhaus, Johnson, Papadimitriou, Seymour & Yannakakis, The complexity of multiterminal cuts, SIAM J. Comput. 23 (1994) 864-894

canonical_task: Power Dominating Set decision: a set of <= k vertices observing all vertices?
citation: Haynes, Hedetniemi, Hedetniemi & Henning, Domination in graphs applied to electric power networks, SIAM J. Discrete Math. 15 (2002) 519-529

canonical_task: RSMT decision: rectilinear Steiner tree of length <= B?
citation: Garey & Johnson, The rectilinear Steiner tree problem is NP-complete, SIAM J. Appl. Math. 32 (1977) 826-834

canonical_task: SCS decision: common supersequence of length <= k?
citation: Raiha & Ukkonen, The shortest common supersequence problem over binary alphabet is NP-complete, TCS 16 (1981) 187-198
note: NP-complete even over a binary alphabet; distinct from shortest-common-superSTRING (substrings, S2)

canonical_task: Strip Packing decision: pack into height <= H?
citation: Baker, Coffman & Rivest, Orthogonal packings in two dimensions, SIAM J. Comput. 9 (1980) 846-855

canonical_task: Tree-metric fitting decision: a tree metric with L-inf error <= e?
citation: Agarwala, Bafna, Farach, Paterson & Thorup, On the approximability of numerical taxonomy (fitting distances by tree metrics), SIAM J. Comput. 28 (1998) 1073-1085

canonical_task: 1||sum w_j T_j decision: a sequence with total weighted tardiness <= V?
citation: Lenstra, Rinnooy Kan & Brucker, Complexity of machine scheduling problems, Annals of Discrete Math. 1 (1977) 343-362
note: strongly NP-hard (unlike unweighted 1||sum T_j, which is only ordinarily NP-hard with a pseudo-poly DP and an FPTAS)

canonical_task: satisfiability of a monotone 2-CNF: trivially satisfiable by the all-true assignment; and 2-SAT is in P in general — a decoupling witness against the hard counting version (cf. #DNF)
citation: Aspvall, Plass & Tarjan, A linear-time algorithm for testing the truth of certain quantified boolean formulas, Inf. Process. Lett. 8 (1979) 121-123
note: 2-SAT in linear time (APT 1979); the monotone case is trivially SAT (all-true)
